page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 224 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4 GB per core. There is no local storage or bundled GPU hardware included with this server configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10% and small-block cached read bandwidth is strong, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier. Cryptographic and database operations also demonstrate strong performance, supported by hardware-level AES and SHA instruction sets.

This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, which align with its strong benchmark results in these areas. It also supports moderate LLM inference tasks, showing strong text generation speeds with medium-sized models, though prompt processing speeds remain average. The lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage, which should be factored into deployment architectures for database or I/O-heavy applications.
